topic: Colour vision deficiency: more common in men; simple facts

youtube.title: Red or green? Are you sure? 🔴🟢 Colour blindness facts #Shorts
youtube.description:
Red or green? Are you sure? Some people really can't tell.
நிறக்குருடு பெண்களை விட ஆண்களுக்கு அதிகம்.

• The retina has three types of colour-sensing cells (cones) for red, green and blue.
• If one type works differently, some colours look alike.
• Studies show about 1 in 12 men, but only about 1 in 200 women, have colour vision deficiency.
• The common type passes down on the X chromosome; men have only one X.
• It's usually present from birth, doesn't get worse and is not blindness.
• A quick colour plate test during an eye test can find it: useful for school and some jobs.
• Colours suddenly looking faded, especially in one eye: see an eye specialist quickly.

gmb.text: Can you always tell red from green? Some people can't, and many don't know it. The retina has three types of colour-sensing cells for red, green and blue; if one type works differently, some colours look alike. Studies show about 1 in 12 men but only about 1 in 200 women have colour vision deficiency, because the common type passes down on the X chromosome and men have only one X. It's usually present from birth, doesn't get worse and is not blindness. A quick colour plate test during an eye test can find it, which helps children at school and matters for some jobs. If colours suddenly look faded, especially in one eye, see an eye specialist quickly. Book an eye test on WhatsApp: 044 4356 9998
